That is already how this site is set up. The bed-management system behind Downstream Out keeps only the patient's current location. It already shows the patient on WARD-C, bay BAY1-07, from the later transfer (event time 09:45 UTC). It has no record of the failed transfer to WARD-B (09:20 UTC).

Not acting, which is the plan: the systems that read the bed-management system are already correct. These are the bed board, pharmacy, porters and the electronic patient record. They see WARD-C, and nothing more is needed.

Acting by resending the failed transfer would move the recorded location back to WARD-B, where the patient no longer is. The bed board would then show the wrong bed. Pharmacy could send medicines to WARD-B. Porters could be asked to move a patient who has already moved.

Only a site that needs a full movement history would want the correction (W1). That means cancelling the WARD-C transfer and resending both transfers in order. The patient would end up on WARD-C again. Under that setting, a person would handle the case. Shutter cannot tell from this case what each of those extra steps would trigger in the other systems.

response.content: I've submitted my answer: the site's patient records already keep only the current placement, so doing nothing leaves every system that reads them showing the patient on WARD-C, while resending the failed transfer would wrongly move the patient back to WARD-B.
